mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with UNRATE > 5.5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal housing sector contraction that reduces household wealth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline.

mechanism_narrative: In manufacturing slowdown regimes (INDPRO growth < 0.5% y/y), a decline in industrial production signals reduced corporate output capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In manufacturing slowdown periods (INDPRO growth < 0.5% y/y), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation that prompts monetary tightening, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL y/y > 3.0%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly employment gains exceeding 100,000 persons (PAYEMS > 100000) signal robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 100000, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (GDP growth > 2.5% annualized), a decline in residential investment (RSAFS) signals housing sector weakness that reduces household wealth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods (GDP growth > 2.5% annualized), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS declines.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1 growth < 1.0% annualized) signal broad economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO declines and GDPC1 growth < 1.0% annualized, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.
